blocks.heading: Truth tables
blocks.text: A truth table lists every combination of truth values for a logical expression and calculates its result. For n propositional variables, there are 2ⁿ rows. For p and q, use TT, TF, FT, and FF.

blocks.heading: Negation
blocks.text: Negation reverses a proposition. p ¬p T F F T p: It is raining. ¬p: It is not raining.

blocks.heading: Conjunction
blocks.text: Conjunction is true only when both parts are true. p q p ∧ q T T T T F F F T F F F F “I will have salad for lunch and rice for dinner” joins two propositions with AND.

blocks.heading: Inclusive OR
blocks.text: Disjunction includes the case where both parts are true. p q p ∨ q T T T T F T F T T F F F “I will go to school or stay home” is an inclusive OR unless “but not both” is specified.

blocks.heading: Exclusive OR
blocks.text: Exclusive OR requires exactly one true part. p q p ⊕ q T T F T F T F T T F F F If p and q say switches A and B are ON, an XOR alarm sounds when exactly one switch is ON.

blocks.heading: Conditional
blocks.text: Implication is false only when a true hypothesis leads to a false conclusion. p q p → q T T T T F F F T T F F T

blocks.heading: Conditional example
blocks.text:
Let p mean “The car is a Rolls-Royce” and q mean “Sarah will buy it.” Then p → q means “If the car is a Rolls-Royce, Sarah will buy it.”

Its truth value depends on p and q; the wording alone does not make it true.

blocks.heading: Biconditional
blocks.text: A biconditional is true for matching truth values. p q p ↔ q T T T T F F F T F F F T p ↔ q means “p if and only if q.”

blocks.heading: Reading a compound expression
blocks.text:
Let p mean “The restaurant is open” and q mean “I have a reservation.”

¬p ∨ q means “The restaurant is not open, or I have a reservation.” Calculate ¬p first, then apply OR.

blocks.heading: Worked truth table: ¬p ∨ q
blocks.text:
<mspace=0.72em>p  q  ¬p  ¬p ∨ q
T  T   F     T
T  F   F     F
F  T   T     T
F  F   T     T</mspace>

The final column matches p → q. Thus p → q and ¬p ∨ q are logically equivalent.

blocks.heading: Worked truth table: (p → q) → ¬q
blocks.text:
<mspace=0.72em>p  q  p → q  ¬q  result
T  T    T     F     F
T  F    F     T     T
F  T    T     F     F
F  F    T     T     T</mspace>

Compute the inner conditional and ¬q before evaluating the outer conditional.
